Work Scale Model

Scale determines how much process is appropriate — a patch and a new project must not follow the same workflow.

The 5 Scales of Work

Project

A Project is the full product or initiative. It uses the full lifecycle: Research, Design, Architecture, Sprint Planning, Build & Test, Review, and Release.

Rule: Scale controls process depth.

Release

A Release is a versioned delivery target — a bounded set of features grouped into one shippable unit (e.g., v0.1 Public Proof).

Rule: A new release updates the project brain. It does not restart the project from zero.

Feature

A Feature is a user-visible or system-visible capability added to an existing project. It may require research, design, validation, and multiple sprints.

Sprint

A Sprint is a bounded AI implementation packet. It typically contains requirements, a blueprint, acceptance criteria, a dry run, and implementation logs. It is the unit that runs through the Sprint Loop.

Rule: A sprint ends when state is updated, not when code compiles.

Patch

A Patch is a small, low-risk change (e.g., fix a typo, update a link). It does not require the full sprint loop.

Rule: Do not run a project process for a patch. Do not run a patch process for a project.
